rationale: Ten acceptance criteria across persona_registry.py, persona_defs.py, personas.py (Persona, build_request, build_prompt, new is_reviewer/declared_settings), the `nw personas` CLI and the capability doc. It is high-end rather than cost-effective because it changes run-request construction and forces read-only/dontAsk permissions, although the queue and the builtin path stay untouched.

findings.title: User personas layer for build_request is unspecified; get_persona defaults to the global config dir, not cfg
findings.detail: The spec writes `p = get_persona(persona, project_root)`. `get_persona` passes `user_dir=None` to `persona_defs.load_registry`, which falls back to `paths.config_dir()/personas`, not `cfg["config_dir"]`. `persona_registry.load_registry` and the request env (`NW_CONFIG_DIR`) use `cfg`. A user-layer declared persona could resolve differently from what `nw personas` lists for that cfg. The Test plan's 'temp user personas dir' also cannot reach build_request without monkeypatching `paths`.
findings.suggested_fix: In Design / build_request, replace the get_persona bullet with: "`p = get_persona(persona, project_root, user_dir=persona_defs.user_personas_dir(cfg))`; `is_reviewer` gets the same `user_dir`." In AC5, add: "a user-layer declared reviewer under `cfg['config_dir']/personas` resolves."
findings.acceptance: build_request and is_reviewer derive user_dir from cfg, and a test puts a declared persona under a tmp cfg config_dir without patching paths.

findings.title: Declared reviewers may use {{tests_touched}} but never get it
findings.detail: `ROLE_PLACEHOLDERS["reviewer"]` allows `tests_touched` (and `campaign_diff`), so the validator accepts a declared reviewer template that uses them. The spec keeps `with_tests = persona == "test_reviewer"`, so `tests_touched` always renders as '(none)' for a declared reviewer. The spec does not say this is intended.
findings.suggested_fix: In Design / build_request, change the with_tests line to: "`with_tests` is `persona == "test_reviewer"` or a declared reviewer (`p.declared is not None and p.role == "reviewer"`), so every placeholder the reviewer role allows is filled." Alternatively, add a sentence that `tests_touched` is not filled for declared reviewers and remove it from `ROLE_PLACEHOLDERS["reviewer"]`.
findings.acceptance: A test renders a declared reviewer template that uses {{tests_touched}} with a tests change and gets non-'(none)' content (or the placeholder is refused by validation).

findings.title: is_reviewer re-scans the registry right after get_persona resolved the persona
findings.detail: `get_persona` and `is_reviewer` each call `persona_defs.load_registry`, which reads and validates every definition file. The role is already on the resolved `p`, so the second scan is redundant.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the review-context bullet to: "Review context: `review = persona in REVIEWER_PERSONAS or (p.declared is not None and p.role == \"reviewer\")` (same answer as `is_reviewer(persona, project_root)`, without a second registry scan)."
findings.acceptance: build_request scans the declared definitions once per call.

findings.title: State that the listed categories include the appended `other`
findings.detail: `reviewer_schema(categories)` appends `other` when it is absent, so a list read from `p.schema` includes `other` even if the definition did not declare it. AC7 and its test should expect this.
findings.suggested_fix: Append to the Generated Output section: "The list includes `other`, which `reviewer_schema` adds when the definition omits it."
findings.acceptance: test_output_section asserts `other` appears in the generated list.

findings.title: template_sha256 source is described as 'bytes read during validation', but validation reads text
findings.detail: `_check_template` uses `read_text(encoding="utf-8")`. Hashing re-encoded text and hashing the raw file can differ (for example a BOM or CRLF handling), so the sentence is ambiguous.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace "The sha256 is of the template bytes read during validation." with "The sha256 is `hashlib.sha256(template_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()` of the template file."
findings.acceptance: The spec names the exact hashing input, and the test compares it against sha256 of the file bytes.
